opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the role owns the Payroll system, the maximum access level is admin. Requested write access is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E031 as a contractor with basic security training (note: HR listed full-time). As a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed access is read. Requested write exceeds this maximum, so recommend read.
reason: There is a conflict between HR (full-time Payroll Specialist) and Security (contractor with basic security training) records for E031. Under the Security record, E031 is a contractor with basic training, so the maximum allowed access to Payroll is read (contractors get read, or write only with advanced training; never admin). The requested write exceeds that maximum, so the granted level is read. I chose the more restrictive interpretation given the conflicting records.
